name: Bauerfield International Airport
before:
Vanuatu's main international gateway, on Efate at Port Vila, and small enough that most arrivals are through the building quickly. The runway is the surprise: it is long and strong enough to take wide body aircraft up to an A330, which is what keeps long haul connections possible from a country of this size.

The airport is formally Port Vila International and almost universally called Bauerfield, a name it carries from the airfield the United States built on the island in 1942, when Efate was fortified to protect the sea route between America and Australia.

One thing to check before quoting: it was the international hub for Air Vanuatu, the national carrier, until the airline went into bankruptcy in 2024. Schedules and connections through Port Vila have been unsettled since, so confirm the operating airline rather than relying on an older route map.
after:
Vanuatu's main international gateway, on Efate at Port Vila. Its paved runway is 2,600 metres long.

The airport is formally Port Vila International but widely known as Bauerfield. It began as an airfield the United States built on Efate in 1942, when the island was fortified to protect the sea route between America and Australia.

One thing to check before quoting: it was the international hub for Air Vanuatu, the national carrier, until the airline collapsed in 2024. Air Vanuatu now flies only domestic routes, while other airlines carry the international traffic, so confirm the operating airline rather than relying on an older route map.

claims.inAfter: Air Vanuatu now flies only domestic routes
claims.note: New, replacing 'Schedules and connections through Port Vila have been unsettled since' (cut below). Air Vanuatu's own site sells only domestic fares from Port Vila (Santo, Tanna, Norsup, Longana and others) and says its fleet of two Twin Otters and one ATR operates on domestic routes; the operator lists it among the domestic airlines and not among the international ones. The sources disagree on one point: the FCDO's advice (still current at 24 September 2026) says Air Vanuatu is not operating international or domestic flights. The airline's and the operator's own current pages are preferred for what the airline flies; the FCDO line agrees that it flies no international routes.

claims.claim: small enough that most arrivals are through the building quickly
claims.wasBefore: and small enough that most arrivals are through the building quickly
claims.why: Wikipedia alone ('relatively small in size'); nothing else says how quickly arrivals clear. The operator mentions only basic shopping and dining in the terminal.

claims.claim: the runway takes wide bodies up to an A330; long haul connections
claims.wasBefore: The runway is the surprise: it is long and strong enough to take wide body aircraft up to an A330, which is what keeps long haul connections possible from a country of this size.
claims.why: Sources disagree. Wikipedia says the runway can take wide-body jets such as the A330; the operator says the airport has been expanded 'to accommodate medium-sized aircraft', and RNZ's report on the 2019 rebuild gives no aircraft size. The operator's international routes are to Australia, New Zealand, Fiji, New Caledonia and the Solomons, none of them long haul. Replaced by the runway's length (see above).

claims.claim: almost universally called Bauerfield, a name it carries from the wartime airfield
claims.wasBefore: The airport is formally Port Vila International and almost universally called Bauerfield, a name it carries from the airfield the United States built on the island in 1942, when Efate was fortified to protect the sea route between America and Australia.
claims.why: Split in two. 'Almost universally' is now 'widely known' (Wikipedia's phrase). That the name comes from the wartime Bauer Field (after Lt-Col Harold W. Bauer) rests on Wikipedia alone: the operator's history says the field was first named Efate Field and does not mention Bauer, and the Navy's history does not name it. The 1942 airfield and its purpose are kept (see above).
